# S619 — spec draft: on the format-fix resume, keep the first report's spec sections when the role returns only its questions, or ask it for the full report

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-26** — Spec draft denial and shape retries now request all five sections and owner questions in one complete reply; the Check line gofmt path now names internal/engine; focused tests, vet and gofmt pass.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

S576 kept the raw report of a failed spec draft. For S614 on 2026-11-26 the kept report shows a draft that failed with "report shape: no block for Why; no block for Files; ...". The role's first reply held the five sections. ork resumed it once, and the role answered with only its owner questions. It wrote that its reply "follows the format you asked for" and "drops the five spec sections". The same failure hit S531, S556, S564, S569, S575, S580 and S588 that week, each costing a full re-draft.

The code explains why the role could think so. When the first round has denied commands, `RunSpecDraft` builds the resume prompt with `specDenialNudge` (`internal/engine/specdraft.go:313`). That function is the spec check's prompt. It asks for one `## Slice ID` section holding `Ready` or `Question:` blocks (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:711-715`). It never mentions `## Section NAME` blocks. A role that follows it sends only its questions, and `ParseSpecDraft` then finds no section blocks. I could not confirm that the S614 failure took this path, because I did not read the kept report. The shape-error nudge at `specdraft.go:321` does name the section blocks, but it does not say that every section must be sent again.

Owner decision, 2026-11-26: Jon chose "File it". The fix is either to reuse the first reply's sections with the resumed questions, or to make the resume prompt ask for the full report including every section. This spec drafts the second option, and the first is raised under Owner needed.

Owner decision, 2026-11-26 (adj 609): prompt fix. The draft gets its own denial nudge, and the shape nudge says every section is sent again; the resumed reply stays the only text ork parses.

## Failing tests

All three go in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go`, using `draftReport`, `specHarness` and `h.runner.requests()`.
- TestSpecDraftDenialResumeAsksForTheSectionBlocks: first result is ExitOK with session sess, draftReport and one denied command. The resumed request must use sess, name the denial, specify ## Section NAME and Why, Files, Failing tests, Implement, Check in order, and ## Owner needed. It must not specify ## Slice, Ready or Question: as the report form. Fails because RunSpecDraft uses specDenialNudge.
- TestSpecDraftShapeResumeAsksForEverySection: first report replaces every ## Section prefix with ##. The resumed brief must include the shape error, require every section again with new text or unchanged even where the earlier report was right, explain that only the resumed reply is read, and put owner questions in the same reply. Fails because the existing shape nudge does not explicitly require repetition.
- TestSpecDraftDenialResumeThatSendsTheFullReportPasses: first result carries a denial; resumed result is draftReport. Assert five parsed sections and no spec-draft-failed-*.md files. This is a compatibility guard; the slice Check section requires it to pass, rather than identifying a pre-change defect.

## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/specdraft.go`, add a constant or helper `specDraftFormat(item string) string` for the report form. It gives the instruction text for one `## Section NAME` block for each of `DraftSections`, in order, each holding the new text or `unchanged`. It then gives the `## Owner needed` section, `none` when nothing is open. It says the whole report goes in one final message as plain text with no code fence. It says every section is sent again even when the earlier report was right, because ork reads only the resumed reply.
2. In `specdraft.go`, add `specDraftDenialNudge(denials []runrec.DeniedCommand, item string) string`. It lists the denied commands as `specDenialNudge` does. That means the same cap of 10, the same "and N more" line and the same one-command-per-call advice. It ends with `specDraftFormat`. Replace the call at `specdraft.go:313` with it. Leave `specDenialNudge` untouched, because the spec check still uses it.
3. In `specdraft.go`, replace the inline shape nudge at line 321 with `"ork checked your report and refused it: " + perr.Error() + "\n\n" + specDraftFormat(cfg.Item)`. Keep the sentence "You may only read the tree. Do not start the draft over; fix the report from what you already read."
4. Add the three tests in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go`.
5. Run `go test ./internal/engine`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .`.
